claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the basics:

**How many children are you inquiring about for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'd like to know if I'm eligible for Child Benefit. I have one child I'm asking about.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility.

**What is your child's name?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Now I have a few questions about Alex to determine eligibility.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. To continue the assessment, I need to understand Alex's current circumstances.

**Is Alex in full-time education or an approved training scheme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask a few more questions about your situation.

**What is your residency status in the UK? Are you a British citizen, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK, yes. I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand your living arrangements with Alex.

**Does Alex live with you as part of your household?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have one more important question about your circumstances.

**Are you responsible for financially supporting Alex, or does Alex have their own income and is self-sufficient?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm responsible for supporting Alex financially.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided:
- Alex is 18 years old
- Alex is not in full-time education or an approved training scheme
- You are a British citizen living in the UK
- Alex lives with you
- You are financially supporting Alex

Unfortunately, under UK Child Benefit rules, eligibility ends when a child reaches 16 years old, unless they are in full-time education (up to age 19) or an approved training scheme. Since Alex is 18 and not currently in education or training, **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry that you're not eligible for Child Benefit in this case. However, if Alex's circumstances change and they begin full-time education or an approved training scheme, that could affect their eligibility. You would be able to claim Child Benefit for them until they turn 19, provided they remain in full-time education or training.

Is there anything else I can help you with?

Child Benefit eligibility requires children to be under 16, or under 19 if in full-time education or an approved training scheme. As Alex does not meet these criteria, they are not eligible for Child Benefit.
